tldr: DEXTERA is a unified real-to-sim-to-real framework that takes a single RGB image of a workspace, automatically reconstructs a 3D Gaussian background and interactive object assets with physical parameters, and trains dexterous manipulation policies in simulation for zero-shot or co-trained deployment on physical multi-fingered robots.
hero_caption: Overview of the single-image asset factorization pipeline for simulator construction. (a) VLM-based foreground/background parsing and physical property inference, (b) 3D mesh generation through segmentation and inpainting, and (c) 3D Gaussian background optimization via image inpainting and multi-view panorama generation, quickly standing up an interactive digital twin.
overview:
Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered robot hands involves complex fingertip contacts and high degrees of freedom. Consequently, collecting data directly in the real world demands immense time, manual labor, and carries hardware damage risks. While scalable data synthesis and policy learning in physics simulators offer a promising alternative, manually building deployment-ready digital twins that mirror the real world is extremely tedious. Furthermore, subtle visual, geometric, and dynamics discrepancies cause a sim-to-real gap that hampers reliable transfer.

To address these hurdles, this paper introduces **DEXTERA**. From just a single RGB image of a tabletop workspace, it automatically factorizes a static 3D Gaussian background, actionable rigid or articulated 3D object meshes, and even physical parameters such as mass and friction inferred by a VLM. It then automatically aligns metric scales and coordinate frames across the camera, robot, and objects, setting up diverse simulation tasks via reusable primitives (lift, push, handover, etc.). VR teleoperation demonstrations are scaled up to thousands of trajectories via object-centric trajectory synthesis, enabling robust policy training via imitation learning and reinforcement learning.

Experiments evaluate DEXTERA across 13 task configurations on two multi-fingered platforms: a single-arm setup (KUKA + LEAP Hand) and a dual-arm setup (OpenArm + BrainCo Hand). Open-loop replay of simulation-successful trajectories on real hardware achieved an 87.95% physical consistency rate. Furthermore, policies trained purely in simulation achieved viable zero-shot real-robot deployment, while simulation-real co-training with a modest amount of physical data substantially boosted mean physical policy success from 29.2% to 61.9%.
contributions: Established a fully automated pipeline factorizing a single RGB image into a 3D Gaussian Splatting background and actionable interactive assets (rigid/articulated, complete with physical properties).
Developed a three-stage automated calibration and alignment method ensuring metric scale, camera extrinsic parameters, and morphology-balanced robot hand-arm alignment.

Introduced scalable simulation task construction and object-centric trajectory synthesis that expand minimal VR demonstrations into large-scale multimodal datasets for imitation and reinforcement learning.

Demonstrated viable zero-shot real-robot deployment from simulation alone and significant physical success rate improvements via co-training (from 29.2% to 61.9%) across 2 multi-fingered platforms and 13 task-embodiment pairs.

sections.heading: Can a single photo teach a dexterous robot hand to manipulate objects?
sections.summary: Because gathering real-world data for dexterous multi-fingered manipulation is exceedingly costly, simulation is indispensable. However, manual environment setup and the sim-to-real gap have long been roadblocks. DEXTERA addresses this by turning a single RGB image into deployable policies end-to-end.
sections.details:
Recent advances in generalist robot foundation models have enabled diverse behaviors across various tasks and embodiments. Yet, training them still relies heavily on human operators teleoperating real hardware, manually resetting failed trials, and monitoring safety—incurring steep real-world costs. In contact-rich dexterous manipulation with high-DOF hands, the required demonstration fidelity and trial count climb even higher.

While physics simulators offer a scalable and safe data collection environment, constructing digital twins that faithfully replicate a given real workspace introduces another major bottleneck. Manually modeling meshes, tuning physical parameters, and calibrating cameras and robots is impractical. Additionally, most existing real-to-sim approaches require multi-view video scans or are confined to simple parallel-jaw pick-and-place tasks, falling short of handling complex multi-fingered contacts.

To overcome this, the authors asked: *Can we reconstruct a visually, geometrically, and physically consistent simulation environment from a single image and train dexterous manipulation policies that transfer directly back to real hardware?* DEXTERA solves this challenge across four unified stages: single-image asset factorization, rigorous metric and morphology calibration, scalable task and trajectory synthesis, and multimodal policy deployment.

sections.heading: Where 3D generative AI meets real-to-sim robot learning
sections.summary: Prior 3D scene synthesis and real-to-sim works primarily focused on visual rendering or two-finger parallel grippers. DEXTERA advances the field by taking a single image input, inferring articulated mechanisms and physical properties, and supporting multi-fingered dexterous hands.
sections.details:
This section organizes related work into three key areas and outlines DEXTERA's distinct positioning.

### II-A 3D Scene Synthesis
Recent neural rendering methods like NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) achieve high-fidelity scene novel view synthesis from sparse captures. However, robot manipulation requires actionable, collision-aware, and metrically accurate representations rather than purely passive visual scenes. DEXTERA factorizes a single image into static backgrounds and actionable foreground assets, inferring articulation and dynamics so that digital assets are immediately interactive in simulation.

### II-B Real-to-Sim for Robot Learning
Real-to-sim systems that ground physical scenes into simulators have gained significant traction, but many rely on multi-view video captures or target specific tasks. Comprehensive frameworks like SimFoundry require multi-view video inputs, while systems like TabletopGen and RoboSnap are restricted to parallel-jaw grippers and tabletop pick-and-place. Automated pipelines taking a single image to contact-rich dexterous multi-fingered manipulation have remained unexplored.

### II-C Simulation-Based Task and Policy Scaling
Modern simulation platforms standardize task creation and domain randomization, but they typically depend on curated pre-existing asset libraries detached from the real tabletop scene at hand. DEXTERA bridges this gap, unifying scene reconstruction, task generation, policy learning, and physical deployment into a single coherent workflow.

sections.heading: Four integrated stages: from one image to physical execution
sections.summary: DEXTERA operates across four stages: (1) single-image asset factorization and 3D generation, (2) metric scene alignment, object canonicalization, and morphology-balanced calibration, (3) task primitive construction, and (4) trajectory synthesis and unified policy learning/deployment.
sections.details:
The input to DEXTERA is a single RGB workspace image $I_{0}$, a robot kinematic model, and sensor readings for calibration (camera intrinsics, robot joint states, and a depth map). Asset generation itself relies solely on $I_{0}$, while the additional measurements ground metric scale and alignment.

### III-A Single-Image Asset Factorization
The input image is first parsed into actionable foreground objects and a static background. A Vision-Language Model, Qwen3-VL, identifies object names, categories, rigid versus articulated types, interactive flags, and estimates physical properties like mass and friction. Foreground instances are segmented via Grounding DINO and SAM 3, unoccluded using FLUX.2, and transformed into textured 3D meshes using Hunyuan3D 3.1. For articulated objects such as scissors or laptops, a feed-forward model predicts part cuts, joint axes, and joint limits, exporting URDF assets. For the background, foreground items are inpainted, HY-World 2.0 expands the view into a panorama, and novel views along virtual camera trajectories optimize a static 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representation.

### III-B Metric Scene and Object Alignment
Because generated assets lack true scale and orientation, they are grounded into real-world metric frames. The 3DGS background scale $s_G$ and camera pose ${}^{G}\mathbf{T}_C$ are optimized against the metric RGB-D frame by minimizing a photometric loss $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{photo}}$ (color and SSIM) and a sparse geometric loss $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{sparse}}$ based on SuperPoint feature matches. For camera-to-robot calibration, DEXTERA introduces **morphology-balanced ICP**: it samples an equal number of points ($N$) from the arm and hand surfaces, preventing the large arm geometry from biasing hand alignment. Generated object meshes are metrically scaled via Sim(3) ICP against observed depth point clouds and oriented into functional canonical frames (e.g., $+Z$ facing functionally upward) via Qwen3-VL reasoning.

### III-C Simulator Task Construction
Aligned assets are loaded into Isaac Lab via USD format. Tasks are composed of six reusable primitives: Lift, Push, Pick and reorient, Pick and place, Handover, and Articulation, complete with automated goal distributions, reward functions, and success detectors. A shared multimodal interface (Table I) separates onboard sensory observations from privileged simulation states, allowing identical observation spaces across simulation and physical robots.

### III-D Policy Learning and Deployment
For demonstration collection, operators collect 10 base VR teleoperation trajectories per task using a Meta Quest 3. These are scaled to thousands of trajectories via object-centric trajectory synthesis (spatial transforms, SLERP interpolation, and Gaussian noise). For imitation learning (ACT, Diffusion Policy, OpenVLA, etc.), co-training mixes simulation and real data in a 1:1 ratio. For reinforcement learning, PPO distillation trains an observation-only student policy from a privileged teacher. Physical deployment is executed in real time via ROS 2.

sections.heading: High fidelity and robust transfer: real-robot dexterous manipulation evaluated
sections.summary: Evaluated on KUKA (LEAP Hand) and OpenArm (BrainCo Revo1) hardware across 13 tasks, DEXTERA outperformed 3D reconstruction baselines, verified physical consistency via an 87.95% open-loop replay success rate, and doubled real-robot policy success from 29.2% to 61.9% with co-training.
sections.details:
Experiments were conducted on two physical setups: a single-arm **KUKA LBR iiwa 7 + LEAP Hand (KL)** and a dual-arm **OpenArm + BrainCo Revo1 (OB)** (Fig. 4).

### IV-A Visual Fidelity and Pose Alignment
Across 86 object instances, DEXTERA was benchmarked against leading generative 3D reconstruction baselines including SAM3D, TRELLIS.2, and Hunyuan3D-2.1 (Table II, Fig. 6). DEXTERA achieved top performance across image mask alignment (Mask IoU), color fidelity (PSNR 25.11 dB), and 3D surface geometry (Chamfer-L1 6.84 mm). The reconstructed background also reached 20.74 dB PSNR and 6.33 mm Chamfer-L1, verifying the high fidelity of the generated digital twins.

### IV-B Physical Consistency through Cross-Domain Replay
To examine whether simulation-successful trajectories hold up physically, 30 trajectories per task (390 total) were executed open-loop on physical hardware. The overall physical replay success rate reached 87.95% (343/390 trials; Table IV, Fig. 7). Notably, four configurations—including bowl handover and dual-arm basket lifting—achieved 100% success. Lower rates occurred in tasks sensitive to contact slip and structural compliance (e.g., reorienting and box placing at 73.33%), confirming that the inferred physical parameters adequately capture real-world dynamics.

### IV-C Policy Learning and Sim-to-Real Transfer
Six policy architectures were tested: ACT, Diffusion Policy (DP), BC-RNN, OpenVLA, $\pi_{0.5}$, and PPO Teacher–Student distillation (Table V). In imitation learning, synthetic simulation data (expanded from 10 VR demos) was co-trained 1:1 with real demos. On real robots, $\pi_{0.5}$ led with a 56.5% average success rate, followed closely by ACT at 54.2%, whereas OpenVLA trailed at 13.8%.

Crucially, zero-shot real-robot deployment from simulation-only training proved viable (Fig. 8). Pure simulation training yielded 35.0% physical success for ACT and 36.7% for $\pi_{0.5}$, reaching 75–80% zero-shot success on closing a laptop. Incorporating a small set of real demos via co-training dramatically improved mean physical policy success from 29.2% to 61.9% (gains observed in 17 out of 18 comparisons). Simulation success also slightly improved from 62.4% to 67.3%, showing that real data co-training benefits simulation generalization as well.

sections.heading: Conclusions and horizons: how far can a single image take us?
sections.summary: DEXTERA proves that single-image inputs can successfully bootstrap and deploy dexterous multi-fingered policies. Current limitations include the absence of deformable or fluid physics and dynamics gaps in long-horizon tasks, outlining clear avenues for future work.
sections.details:
This work presented DEXTERA, an integrated pipeline spanning single-image asset factorization, rigorous geometric and physical alignment, task construction, trajectory synthesis, and multimodal policy deployment. Evaluated across 13 dexterous manipulation task pairs, it demonstrated an 87.95% cross-domain trajectory replay success rate, viable zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, and a major boost in physical policy performance via co-training (29.2% to 61.9%).

The authors also candidly highlight several key limitations and open frontiers:
- Asset factorization is restricted to rigid and articulated bodies, without support for deformable objects (e.g., cloth) or fluids.
- Evaluations focus on fundamental task primitives; testing extended, long-horizon multi-stage workflows remains future work.
- VLM-inferred physical parameters still exhibit errors, which can compound into dynamics drift in multi-step placement tasks.
- While background synthesis scales to room-sized environments, current physical validation is limited to stationary robot bases; extending to mobile manipulation is needed.
- Robot kinematic models and URDFs are assumed to be known apriori rather than inferred directly from the image.

Despite these boundaries, demonstrating that a single photograph can automatically construct an operational, high-contact dexterous manipulation environment represents a significant milestone toward fully autonomous robot learning.

takeaways: Combining cutting-edge 3D generative AI with VLM-based physical parameter inference makes it possible to build contact-ready simulation environments from just a single RGB image.
Meticulous metric alignment—such as morphology-balanced ICP that equalizes arm and hand points, combined with hybrid photometric/geometric optimization—is essential for closing the sim-to-real gap.
While pure simulation training enables over 30% zero-shot real-robot transfer, co-training with a modest set of physical demonstrations doubles physical success rates to over 60%.
limitations: Supports only rigid and articulated objects, lacking simulation and generation capabilities for deformable items (e.g., garments, sponges) or fluids.
In long-horizon tasks requiring multiple sequential steps, minor inaccuracies in VLM-estimated physical parameters can compound and lead to manipulation failures.
Assumes the robot's own URDF kinematics and geometry are pre-known rather than automatically reconstructed from the workspace image.
